cards.title: Why One AI Researcher Still Doubts True Recursive Self-Improvement
cards.why_it_matters: As an AI/research engineer, this is a technically grounded dissent against the current 'singularity soon' bandwagon — directly relevant to how you should weigh RSI claims and safety discourse in 2025–26.
cards.summary: The author argues against true RSI via three claims: automatable research is too narrow to overcome exponential scaling costs, parallel agents face real diminishing returns, and resource/political bottlenecks remain largely AI-resistant. They expect things to move fast enough to feel like short-timeline advocates were right, but predict no superintelligence within 8 years — framing current safety anxiety as culturally amplified rather than evidence-driven.
